tpStops: Thuan Phuoc Bridge is the last crossing on the Han River before Da Nang Bay, about 1,856 m long.
The aerodynamic steel box girder is welded from 69 segments; 27 m of clearance lets ships into the bay.
Two reinforced-concrete towers rise 80 m above their bases, with crossbeams at the top and beneath the deck.
The two 360 mm main cables pass over saddles; an aviation light blinks on each tower.
Twelve 50 m prestressed-concrete spans on each side slope down to Nguyen Tat Thanh Street and the Son Tra peninsula.
Son Tra peninsula lies to the east; 114 hangers about 9.9 m apart tie the main cables to the girder.
At night LEDs on the cables, hangers and towers shift through blue, purple, pink and green, flowing along the bridge like wind heading out to sea.
shStops: Opened on 29 March 2000, the 487.7 m Han River Bridge links Le Duan Street with Pham Van Dong Street.
The 122.7 m centre span rotates 90° around a round pier. The tour swings the bridge once at 30× speed.
The swing span rests on a rail ring and rollers around the pier; a king pin keeps it centred as it turns.
When open, the span lies along the river, leaving two channels for ships on either side of the pier.
Before swinging, the signals turn red and barriers drop at both ends of the span; vehicles already on it drive off.
Its mast is taller than the ~11 m clearance, so it can only pass when the bridge is open. In real life the bridge swings at 23:00 on Saturday and Sunday nights.
ttlStops: A sail on the Han River
The 731 m Tran Thi Ly Bridge has a single pylon leaning west like a sail filled with wind.
The 145 m concrete pylon rises 134 m above the deck and leans away from the 230 m main span to balance the pull of the cables.
Instead of being fixed to the pier, the pylon stands on two steel bearings, each carrying about 250,000 kN.
At night LEDs on the pylon, cables and deck shift through red, pink, purple and blue.
A single semi-fan plane on the centreline anchors in the 5.5 m median of the main span; the 34.5 m deck carries six lanes.
In the two rear planes the highest cable anchors nearest the pylon and the lowest farthest away, forming a hyperbolic surface seen from below.
Just to the north is the old steel truss bridge, now for pedestrians only.
swingAuto: Swings automatically at 23:00 on Saturdays and Sundays (Vietnam time) and stays open for 30 minutes.

stops: The 666 m Dragon Bridge links downtown Hai Chau (west bank) with Son Tra district and My Khe Beach (east bank).
A curling tail with flared fins at the west end, facing the city centre.
Six traffic lanes, three each way; a 6 m central median; 2.5 m sidewalks on both sides. 37.5 m wide in total.
The dragon’s body rises highest over the central span. Steel hangers tie its belly to the deck.
Five main spans rest on piers in the riverbed; tour boats pass beneath.
The head faces the sea. At 21:00 on Saturday and Sunday nights the dragon breathes fire, then sprays water.
A 731 m cable-stayed bridge with a single 145 m pylon leaning 12°; its three cable planes form a sail filled with wind.
Seen from the river mouth. Son Tra Mountain lies to the northeast, the Hai Van range to the northwest.
